_about: RATIFIED Company Standard for LIABILITY-MSA-001 — the MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
liability position. Owner decisions of 2026-08-19: Q3=B (per-type standards) and
'MSA standard = 6 months from MSA.pdf §17.2'. It is CONFIGURATION, not
specification: no all_lock.md entry, no locked decision amended.
Single source of truth: corpus fixtures reference it by `company_standard_ref`
rather than repeating the values, so the standard cannot drift between cases.
⚠️ THE SOURCE TEMPLATE CONTRADICTS ITSELF, and the owner chose the operative
clause. MSA.pdf §17.2 caps at six months of fees for the specific Services
giving rise to the claim; §17.7 caps at total fees over a BLANK number of
months. The owner ruled on 2026-08-18 that the two clauses govern one scope and
contradict (fixture DOC-LIAB-04 pins CONFLICT for the document read as a
whole), and on 2026-08-19 that §17.2 is the standard's source. A blank period
cannot state a position, so §17.7 could not serve. The contradiction remains a
defect in the outbound template, reported to the owner for fixing on paper.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT CONTAIN, deliberately:
No acceptable_max, no approval_required_above, no unlimited_outcome, and no
Legal Rule of any kind. None is approved (owner, 2026-08-18). A deviation is
therefore NEVER automatically acceptable, approval-requiring or unacceptable:
rule_outcome stays NOT_APPLICABLE (locked Step 20 r4) and the Evaluation is
routed to a human -- see UNRULED_DEVIATION_REQUIRES_DECISION in
legalmind/evaluation/workflow.py.
source_document: Leapswitch Master Services Agreement, Version 2 (July 2025) — MSA.pdf at LEGALMIND_SOURCE_MATERIAL_DIR
source_quote: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, the total aggregate liability of Leapswitch and its affiliates, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total amount actually paid by the Customer to Leapswitch for the specific Services giving rise to the claim during the six (6) month period immediately preceding the event giving rise to such liability.

FEES_PAID_FOR_AFFECTED_SERVICES: for the specific services giving rise to the claim

_semantics: unit MONTHS with preferred 6 encodes the LOOKBACK WINDOW the clause states
('during the six (6) month period immediately preceding the event'). It is NOT
a multiplier of a monthly fee; the two diverge under non-monthly billing. Same
reading as the ToS standard, reported to the owner on 2026-08-18.
basis FEES_PAID_FOR_AFFECTED_SERVICES means fees paid for the specific Services
giving rise to the claim — the clause's own seven-word restriction. It is
deliberately DISTINCT from FEES_PAID (total fees, the ToS basis): the owner
ruling of 2026-08-18 keeps the two incomparable, so a counterparty cap measured
on total fees fails closed against this standard rather than being compared
numerically. Do not add either to comparable_bases or a conversion rule without

evaluation_rules._note: comparison semantics live in tested code (44.29); deviation disposition lives in the Legal Rule, never here

_terminology: Mapping and extraction terminology, added 2026-08-19 under the owner's
publishability tasking (AUTO_MODE_DECISIONS.md #18-#21). Every term is drawn
from the cited source clause's own wording or names the clause type
generically; no term encodes a legal position (rules 7/21 - positions live
in `configuration`, sourced above). confirm_threshold 5 is STRUCTURAL: one
exact phrase confirms, or a section heading plus a keyword group. Locked
35.9 fixes no threshold and 35.10 requires calibration against a
representative contract set before the value is trusted; recalibration is a
new mapping rule version (data), never a code change.
_legal_rule_note: APPROVED ZERO-TOLERANCE LEGAL RULE (manager ruling 2026-08-19; owner
approval to wire, 2026-08-20). MATCH -> ACCEPTABLE (no decision needed);
ANY deviation -- unlimited included -> UNACCEPTABLE -> Legal Decision
required; nothing that differs is ever auto-approved. There are
deliberately NO thresholds and NO tolerance bands: do not add
acceptable_max or approval_required_above, and do not ask for them --
the policy is that none exists. Wired as deviation_outcome +
unlimited_outcome, both read by the evaluators; an unrecognised value
fails closed to NOT_APPLICABLE and a human (ENG-09, Step 20 r4).
